page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-8 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware. The CPU architecture supports instruction sets such as AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, but lacks AVX-512 and AMX capabilities.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing the instance in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench scores, and Passmark CPU metrics generally align with average tier expectations. Memory subsystem performance shows a contrast, with cached small-block read bandwidth reaching 508.47 GB/sec, while Passmark memory scores and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the bottom 25% tier. Static web serving throughput averages 7.56 GB/sec, and small-scale LLM inference using a 135M model achieves average processing speeds.

The n2d-highcpu-8 offers a cost-efficient profile for CPU-heavy tasks that do not require large memory footprints, given its dedicated AMD EPYC cores and low RAM-to-vCPU ratio. However, the 8.0 GB memory limitation and weak multi-threaded decompression performance represent significant tradeoffs for memory-intensive applications. This configuration is best suited for compute-bound workloads such as software compilation, ray tracing, web serving, and lightweight text or image processing.
